question: What actually picks up the dirt?
scope: Illustrative bagged cleaner. Not an exact appliance or a measured simulation.

beats.title: A fan makes air move.
beats.explanation: The motor turns a fan. Moving air out lowers the pressure inside, so room air flows in.
beats.narration: An electric motor turns a fan. The fan moves air out, lowering air pressure inside the cleaner. That gives room air a reason to flow in.

beats.title: Moving air carries loose dirt.
beats.explanation: Room air enters through the nozzle and hose. Loose dirt travels with it.
beats.narration: Air flows through the nozzle and hose, carrying loose dirt with it. Blue markers stand for air; dark specks stand for dirt.

beats.title: Air passes through. Dirt stays.
beats.explanation: A porous bag catches dirt. Air passes through the bag material, then continues to the fan and outlet.
beats.narration: A porous bag catches dirt while letting air through its material. The air continues to the fan and leaves through the outlet.

beats.title: One open path. Three jobs.
beats.explanation: These jobs happen together. The chapters only change what we look at.
beats.narration: The fan moves air. The air carries dirt. The bag keeps it. These jobs happen together, along one open path.

experiment.title: Still turning. No fresh dirt coming in.
experiment.explanation: With the inlet sealed, there is no sustained throughflow to carry fresh dirt. A running motor is not enough.
experiment.narration: The fan is still turning. But with the inlet sealed, there is no continuous air path to carry fresh dirt in. A running motor is not enough.
